name: Build a competitor battlecard from their pages and G2 reviews with Bright Data, GPT-5.6 and Google Docs

parameters.content:
## Build a competitor battlecard from their own pages and their own reviews

Fill in a competitor's website and your product. A few minutes later a Google Doc lands in your Drive with their pricing, their claims, and the complaints their customers put in writing - every line traceable to a page.

### How it works

Two lanes run at once. **Their side**: a **Bright Data SERP** search finds their pricing, customers and case-study pages, and the **Web Unlocker** fetches each one. **The customers' side**: a second search finds their G2 profile, which is fetched the same way.

G2 is the review source on purpose. Measured while this was built: G2 returns ten complete reviews written around its own *what do you like / what do you dislike* prompts, while Trustpilot cuts every review off at `See more` even with rendering on, and Capterra returned nothing.

The lanes meet at **`Combine Both Halves`**, GPT-5.6 writes the card, and **`Check Every Quote`** then drops any quote it cannot find in the fetched text and tells you how many it dropped.

The card is written to a new **Google Doc**, the link goes to Slack, and the person who filled the form gets it back in their browser.

### Setup

1. Bright Data: a SERP zone and a Web Unlocker zone, as one Header Auth credential. Free tier is 5,000 credits a month, no card.

2. An OpenAI credential, a Google Docs credential and a Slack credential.

3. In **Settings**, leave `drive_folder_id` as `root` to write to the top of your Drive, or paste a folder ID.

4. Open the Form Trigger, copy its URL, and give it to whoever asks you for battlecards.

## 1. One form, two questions
A competitor's domain and what you sell. Everything else is looked up, so the person asking does not have to know where the competitor publishes anything.

## 2. Two searches, side by side
Their own pages above, their G2 profile below. The slug is never guessed - monday.com is `monday-com`, so the URL comes out of the search.

## 3. Fetch both, read both
G2 returns ten complete reviews around its own like/dislike prompts. Trustpilot cuts every review off at `See more`, even rendered, which is why it is not here.

## 4. The model sees one thing
Both lanes are folded into a single evidence pack. Building it here rather than in the prompt is what lets the check below compare quotes against exactly what was shown.

## 5. Write it, then check it
Every quote has to be findable in the fetched pages. Lines whose quote is not there are dropped and counted, because this gets read out in front of a customer.

## 6. Plain text, on purpose
A Google Docs insert writes the string it is given. Markdown is not parsed, so headings are rebuilt out of capitals and blank lines before the document is created.

## 7. Where it lands
The link goes to the channel, and whoever filled the form gets the card back in their browser rather than a blank confirmation page.

## This is a research brief, not a claim you can make publicly

Everything here comes from the competitor's own marketing and from ten reviews on one site. Ten reviews are not their customer base, G2's sample skews toward customers a vendor asked to review them, and a pricing page rarely shows the discount a rep will offer. Read the card as *what to ask about on the call*, not as facts you can put in an ad.

**Comparative advertising is regulated.** Repeating a customer's complaint back to a prospect in conversation is ordinary selling. Publishing it as a claim about a named competitor is a different thing in most countries, and neither this workflow nor the model knows which one you are about to do.

The quote check is a string match against the pages that were fetched. It proves a sentence was on the page; it does not prove the sentence is true, current, or representative.

One run is roughly eight Bright Data requests. The form is open to anyone who has the URL, so put it behind n8n's form authentication before you share it widely.

parameters.text:
=Write a sales battlecard about a competitor, using only the evidence below.

The competitor: {{ $json.brand }} ({{ $json.domain }})
What we sell: {{ $json.your_product }}
Where we keep losing to them: {{ $json.losing_on }}

Write these sections and nothing else, each as a short markdown heading followed by bullets:

## How they position themselves
Two or three bullets, in their own words where possible.

## What they charge
Their tiers and prices exactly as the evidence gives them. If the evidence has no prices, write one bullet saying prices were not published.

## What their customers praise
Two or three bullets, each ending with a short direct quote in double quotes taken word for word from a LIKE block.

## What their customers complain about
Three bullets, each ending with a short direct quote in double quotes taken word for word from a DISLIKE block. These are the objections to raise.

## Questions to ask a prospect who is evaluating them
Four questions that follow from the complaints above.

## Where we are weak against them
Be honest. If the evidence shows they are genuinely better at something, say so plainly.

Rules: every double-quoted string must be copied character for character from the evidence. Never quote anything that is not there. Do not mention any company the evidence does not mention. No preamble, no closing line.

EVIDENCE
{{ $json.evidence }}
